about.title:
From code
to the SOC
about.p1: I learned to program at 42 Luxembourg, a school without teachers or lectures. You get a project, you build it, and other students review your code. I graduated in March 2026.
about.p2: I have worked with blockchain and Solidity for more than two years. I’m one of the co-founders of Zaori Capital, a regulated fintech that tokenizes real-world assets, and I worked on its platform myself. Security is part of every feature there: identity checks before anyone can hold a token, secrets kept out of the code, and smart contracts that cannot be patched once deployed.
about.p3: That work made me curious about what happens after the code ships: who watches the systems, and what they do when something goes wrong. So I completed the Common Core at DLH Academy, moved on to its defensive track, and started a cybersecurity degree at Unigran Europa. I practise in my own lab and, through November 2026, on a proof of concept during my internship at BCE.
